newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid summer heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid summer heat.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Tuesday, led by warmer-than-normal weather across many parts of the U.S., industry sources said.
July, which is set to expire Thursday, traded from $2.25 to $2.265 in over-the-counter business. This followed Monday's settlement at $2.246 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 0.4 cent firmer at $2.25.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked unchanged at $2.28-2.30 per mmBtu.

Technically, traders said resistance in July was at $2.275, and then at $2.30, $2.36-2.37 and the contract high of $2.44. Support was seen at $2.215, and then at the $2.151 double bottom, $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In Monday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to about $2.10, while New York city gate gas was quoted almost 10 cents higher in the high-$2.50s.
As above-normal temperatures stretched across the East, Midwest and Southwest, traders also said the unscheduled absence of some nuclear power was contributing to the supportive market.

In the Northeast, PECO's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 1 nuclear unit and GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 unit were expected to remain shut for about a week. Indian Point's units 2 and 3, totalling 1,940 MW, were also off line in New York for refueling and maintenance.

Meanwhile in the Southeast, Duke Power's three units--Oconee 1 (846 MW), Oconee 3 (846 MW) and McGuire 2 (1,129 MW)--were also off line. TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar unit was operating at 80 percent power, while the 812 MW Farley 1 unit, in Alabama, was cut to 65 percent for repairs.
However, a sharp uptick in prices may be tempered by the anticipated drop in demand in the first week of July due to the Independence Day holiday, traders said.
